run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:05:47Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for frontend-proxy fires because frontend-proxy returned HTTP 500/504 for the /api/data route (frontend -> ad service) while every other route kept succeeding. Frontend-proxy's error spans jumped from a background 0-4/min to 90-126/min in the minutes 01:09:00-01:16:00 and then returned to 0. The failures originate one hop down: the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls failed two ways - fast (0.3-0.5 ms) with grpc code 14 UNAVAILABLE 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080', which is the ad Service ClusterIP, and slow, where ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span took 22-28 s because its flagd ResolveBoolean child calls took 0.4-4.4 s and ended DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, pushing frontend /api/data past frontend-proxy's 15 s egress timeout (504). Both signatures begin right after the ad Deployment's only replica was replaced: Deployment otel-demo/ad was rolled at 01:07:07 (ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 created, ad-554b849958 scaled to 0, pod created 01:07:07 and old pod killed 01:07:09), with an unchanged pod template (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, same env and same resources), i.e. a restart annotated kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:07:07Z. The replacement ad container reports running since 01:07:09 with 0 restarts and has no readiness/liveness/startup probe, yet its application log only begins at 2026-11-17T01:11:56.907Z with 'Ad service starting.', and ad responses stayed 5-28 s slow until roughly 01:16 before normal request handling at 01:17:36-01:17:57. Established: what broke is the ad service tier reachable from frontend; supported but not proven: the ad restart is the trigger and the container's 50m CPU limit is the reason the replacement stayed unavailable/slow. The reason the deployment was restarted, and any CPU-throttling data, could not be obtained. Hypotheses kept open: ad container CPU starvation (limit 50m, request 10m) after restart; the flagd-config 'adFailure' fault flag, which is set to 'on' but whose declared failure mode does not match the observed transport-level failures; and an ad-side delay in the ad->flagd path, since flagd server spans themselves completed in 9-110 microseconds.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span error rate rose sharply: STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation 'ingress' went from a background 0-4 per minute to 108 (01:09:00), 110, 90, 122, 100, 102, 54 (01:15:00) and back to 0 at 01:16:00, with 'router frontend egress' following the same curve; these are the errors behind the RequestErrorRate alert.

The failing responses are frontend-proxy ingress spans with http.status_code 504 (about 15 s duration), 503 and 500, and the corresponding 'router frontend egress' spans to the frontend with error=true and http.status_code 0, i.e. failures waiting on the frontend upstream, not internal frontend-proxy errors.

The errors are confined to the ad path: in the frontend service, STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans appear only on operation 'GET', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' and 'tcp.connect', while GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, /api/products/{productId} and /api/recommendations show no error spans.

One sampled error trace shows the exact timeout chain: load-generator GET 504 -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 lasting 15.00 s -> frontend /api/data 24.59 s -> frontend grpc GetAds 24.59 s -> ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 22.37 s, inside which ad's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean client spans took 1.60 s, 3.60 s and 2.30 s and returned rpc.grpc.status_code 4, with one flagd server span carrying otel.status_description 'context deadline exceeded'.

A second, faster failure signature exists: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans fail in 299-490 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080', producing frontend GET /api/data 500 and frontend-proxy ingress 500; those traces contain no ad service spans at all, so the request never reached the ad application.

100.70.197.56 is the ad Service ClusterIP (service 'ad', port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad); the pod IPs are in 100.96.x.x (current ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh = 100.96.3.224), so the ECONNREFUSED target is the service VIP, consistent with the service having no accepting backend at the time of the last connection attempt.

frontend's GetAds p90 latency per 2-minute window is 63-128 ms from 01:02 to 01:10, collapses to 1.9-2.0 ms at 01:12 and 01:14 (the instant-ECONNREFUSED path), spikes to 15000 ms at 01:16 (the 15 s frontend-proxy egress timeout path) and then falls to 545/199/264 ms at 01:18/01:20/01:22.

Deployment otel-demo/ad was rolled during the incident: events record Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' at 01:07:07 and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' at 01:07:09, with ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 SuccessfulCreate, pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh Created/Started 01:07:08-09 and old pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc Killing at 01:07:09.

The ad rollout did not change the pod template: old ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 and new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, the same env (AD_PORT 8080, FLAGD_HOST flagd, FLAGD_PORT 8013, OTEL_*) and the same resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi); the only template difference is the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:07:07Z, so the rollout was a restart of the workload, not a configuration change.

The replacement ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh runs with restartCount 0 and container state running since 2026-11-17T01:07:09Z, has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, and its application stdout begins only at 2026-11-17T01:11:56.907Z with the line 'Ad service starting.', after which request logging continues (e.g. 'Targeted ad request received for [accessories]' through 01:17:57).

The ad->flagd delay is on the ad side, not in flagd's handler: in the same traces, ad's ResolveBoolean client spans last 0.4-4.4 s and end with rpc.grpc.status_code 4, while the matching flagd server spans (service 'flagd', v0.12.8) complete in 9-110 microseconds, mostly with rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 (success) in the sampled 01:14:20-01:14:54 traces, and the ad span-metric error counters for GetAds/getAdsByCategory/getRandomAds are 0 throughout 00:50-01:25 (only one flagd EventStream error span at 01:05), so no application-level ad failure is observed; the impact is latency and transport unreachability.

Other services show no error spans in the same window: per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR counts for accounting, cart, checkout, currency, email, payment, product-catalog and shipping are 0, while ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each show only a single span-level blip (1.11); the errors are concentrated in frontend (peak 1137) and frontend-proxy (peak 481).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) contains a fault-injection flag 'adFailure' with defaultVariant 'on' and description 'Fail ad service'; every other flag (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) defaults to off.

flagd itself is up and ready: pod flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr (containers flagd and flagd-ui) is Running with all containers ready and 0 restarts, and service flagd (ClusterIP 100.66.18.32) has endpoint 100.96.3.202; the flagd pod was rolled earlier, at 00:36:53 (ReplicaSet flagd-5466bf5bc replacing flagd-c47676d99 with an identical pod template).

frontend-proxy is serving normally on the other routes in the same period: its access log is dominated by 200 responses for /api/products, /api/recommendations, /api/cart, /api/checkout and /api/data (e.g. at 01:14:46-01:14:57 and 01:17:56-01:17:58), and its 308 redirect spans stay error-free, so the frontend-proxy error signal comes from the /api/data -> ad path only.

The 01:07:07 restart of Deployment ad is the event that started the incident: it replaced the only ad replica (old pod killed 01:07:09, new pod created 01:07:07), the replacement container only began serving at 01:11:56, and the frontend's fast ECONNREFUSED-to-ad-ClusterIP 500s plus the later 5-28 s ad responses fit that gap and its aftermath; what triggered the restart cannot be determined without change history.

The ad container's CPU limit of 50m (request 10m) is a plausible cause of both the ~5 minute delay before 'Ad service starting.' and the 5-28 s GetAds latencies: the ad process spent 0.4-4.4 s per flagd resolve while flagd answered in 9-110 microseconds, which points to client-side CPU scheduling rather than flagd processing; this is unverified because no container CPU/throttling metric series is available in this target.

The enabled fault-injection flag 'adFailure' (description 'Fail ad service') in ConfigMap flagd-config is a candidate fault source, but it does not match the observed failure path: failing calls never reached the ad application (no ad spans, code 14 ECONNREFUSED) and the ad spans that did run returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 rather than an application error, so its contribution to this incident is unproven.

frontend-proxy and frontend are not themselves the origin of the errors: frontend-proxy's ingress error spans are 504/500 responses after its 15 s egress wait on the frontend, and the frontend's spans show it was blocked inside its AdService/GetAds call; all other frontend routes and other services had zero error spans in the window.

flagd is not evidenced as the failing component: its pod is running and ready with 0 restarts, its service has a live endpoint, and in the incident traces its ResolveBoolean server spans completed in 9-110 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 while only the ad-side client spans timed out, so a flagd-wide outage is not supported by its own spans.

A frontend-proxy-internal or cluster-network-blocking fault is not supported: frontend-proxy served 200/308 for all non-ad routes through the incident, and the ad Service kept a valid endpoint (100.96.3.224) targeting the running pod, so the 500s are explained by the ad backend not accepting connections rather than by frontend-proxy itself.

Add a readiness probe to the ad container (or otherwise gate traffic) so the Service does not send requests to a pod whose application has not started listening, and review the ad Deployment's 50m CPU limit against its observed warm-up and per-request cost.

Confirm with cluster audit/change history who or what applied the kubectl rollout restart to Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T01:07:07Z (restartedAt annotation) and whether the flagd-config 'adFailure' flag was intentionally turned on, since the change-history integration was not available in this Run.

gaps: Change history is not integrated (data_sources.not_integrated: change_history), so what triggered the Deployment otel-demo/ad restart at 01:07:07 (restartedAt annotation) is unknown.

No container CPU/throttling series (for example container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) was returned by get_metric_names for this target, so ad CPU starvation from its 50m limit is unverified; the get_metric_names query on {__name__=~".*flagd.*|.*kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total.*"} returned nothing.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate could not be read (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so its exact expression/window and why it fired at 01:05:47Z, before the 01:09 error burst, are unknown.

flagd application logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs on flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr (containers init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) returned no lines both unfiltered and with an error filter, so flagd-side symptoms remain unobserved at log level.

flagd has no series in traces_span_metrics_calls_total (service_name values returned: accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping), and get_series for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name="ad"} returned nothing, so ad/flagd latency cannot be tracked through those metrics.
The frontend pod's logs returned no data (frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw, container frontend: 0 lines in 01:00-01:25), so frontend-side runtime errors are unverified beyond its spans.
Logs of the terminated ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc are unavailable (pod deleted at 01:07:09; container has no previous instance), so the pre-restart ad behaviour at 01:07 cannot be inspected.

Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in otel-demo returned no items; an empty result only shows those selectors matched nothing, so the absence of a blocking NetworkPolicy or quota is not proven.
Jaeger only retains the most recent traces, so trace evidence covers roughly 01:14:20-01:19:28; the 01:09-01:14 fast-failure period is documented here through span metrics only.
Whether the ad Service had zero ready endpoints between 01:07:09 and ~01:11:56 cannot be verified after the fact; the endpoint list shows only the new pod now.
next_steps: Pull Kubernetes audit logs / change history for Deployment otel-demo/ad around 2026-11-17T01:07:07Z to identify who or what performed the rollout restart.
Query container CPU throttling and CPU usage for pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (and its predecessor) for 01:00-01:30 to test the 50m-limit starvation hypothesis.
Check flagd's own metrics/logs (flagd_evaluations_*, gRPC server latency) if a scrape job can be enabled, and confirm whether the adFailure flag in ConfigMap flagd-config was intentionally enabled.
Review whether the ad Deployment should have a readiness probe and a higher CPU limit before the next rollout of its single replica.

flagd is not evidenced as the failing component: its pod is running and ready with 0 restarts, its service has a live endpoint, and in the incident traces its ResolveBoolean server spans completed in 9-110 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 while only the ad-side client spans timed out, so a flagd-wide outage is not supported by its own spans.

rejected_hypothesis.text: A frontend-proxy-internal or cluster-network-blocking fault is not supported: frontend-proxy served 200/308 for all non-ad routes through the incident, and the ad Service kept a valid endpoint (100.96.3.224) targeting the running pod, so the 500s are explained by the ad backend not accepting connections rather than by frontend-proxy itself.
